patients.label: 52-year-old man with glioblastoma multiforme who died with liver and bone marrow toxicity after dichloroacetate and artesunate
attribution_limitations: The abstract says the patient died 10 days after the infusion, while the timeline places the infusion 148 days and death 157 days after surgery (9 days). This is an arithmetic or rounding difference; both are kept and neither is resolved.

RUCAM table cells carry criterion wording that does not match other statements: the risk-factor row prints an age of 55 years or more while the patient is described as 52 years old; "no hypotension" is listed among non-drug causes while hypotension is described later; "Decrease <50% within 30 days" is scored although the patient died; "No information" for concomitant drugs sits beside a stable/unchanged concomitant medication statement. Each cell is kept as printed and none is reconciled.
The authors suspected liver toxicity by valproic acid or temozolomide at hospitalization; "or" asserts neither drug, and they then call this possibility rather unlikely.

The authors consider aspiration pneumonia or spontaneous internal bleeding as possible causes of the sudden blood pressure decline and say the cause of death remains speculative; no cause is asserted.
Causation of the liver and bone marrow toxicity by the DCA and ART combination is hedged ("can be assumed", "can be speculated", "reasonable probability"); it is not recorded as an asserted cause.

The source states both that the concomitant medication was stable/unchanged at the time of infusion and, in RUCAM, that there was no information on concomitant drugs; the drug list itself is not given beyond the antiepileptics and steroids described earlier.

The discussion cites "the prior normal values" without naming the analyte; they may refer to the leukocyte and thrombocyte counts or to the liver values relevant to the VA or TMZ hypothesis, so the fact is kept review_only.

claims.text: A 52-year-old man was diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme after several weeks of cognitive decline, headaches, gait ataxia and a series of epileptic seizures. Radiotherapy up to 60 Gy with simultaneous temozolomide began 53 days after surgery, delayed by complicated wound healing. His general state was unfavorable, with a Karnofsky score of 50 and right-side hemiparesis, so adjuvant temozolomide was ruled out and rehabilitation started.
